content.value_statement: Apple platform projects need shared design context before HIG guidance is useful. This skill gathers product, platform, technology, accessibility, and design details into a reusable context document.
actual_capabilities: Checks for an existing Apple design context document before asking new questions.
Discovers context from README files, Swift packages, Xcode projects, Info.plist, source code, assets, and accessibility markers.
Asks structured questions about product stage, platforms, technology, design system, accessibility, users, and design assets.
Generates an Apple Design Context document with product, platform, technology, design, accessibility, and user sections.
Updates changed sections while preserving existing context information.
limitations: It does not validate Apple HIG compliance by itself.
It depends on available project files and user confirmation for accuracy.
It creates design context, not production Swift or interface code.
It may miss design decisions stored outside the repository.

use_cases.title: Start a New Apple App
use_cases.description: Capture platform, technology, and accessibility goals before requesting HIG guidance.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Design Review
use_cases.description: Document design system choices, supported platforms, and user contexts for focused Apple guideline feedback.

use_cases.title: Align Engineering Decisions
use_cases.description: Record frameworks, minimum OS versions, and architecture details used by related HIG skills.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up my Apple design project context for a new iOS app. Ask only the essential questions first.

prompt_templates.title: Update Existing Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my existing Apple design context and update only the sections that changed for this redesign.

prompt_templates.title: Discover Context from Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the project files for Apple platform, framework, asset, and accessibility signals. Present findings for confirmation before writing context.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Multi-Platform Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a detailed Apple design context for an app targeting iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS with accessibility and design system notes.

output_examples.input: Set up project context for a SwiftUI productivity app on iOS and macOS.
output: Summarizes the app purpose, stage, and category.
Lists target platforms, minimum operating systems, and framework choices.
Captures design system, accessibility, user, and challenge notes for later HIG guidance.

output_examples.input: Update my context after adding visionOS support and stronger accessibility goals.
output: Identifies the affected platform and accessibility sections.
Asks for missing details before editing.
Preserves unchanged product, design system, and user information.

output_examples.input: Discover what you can from this Apple app repository before asking me questions.
output: Reviews project files for platform, framework, asset, and accessibility signals.
Requests only the remaining information needed for a complete context document.

best_practices: Confirm discovered project details before generating the context document.
Keep platform support, minimum OS versions, and accessibility goals current.
Run related HIG skills after the context document is updated.
anti_patterns: Skipping user confirmation when project files are incomplete.
Using one context document for unrelated products.
Treating the context document as a final HIG compliance audit.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates or updates a shared Apple design context document for related HIG skills.

faq.question: Does it replace Apple HIG review?
faq.answer: No. It prepares context so other guidance can be more specific and useful.

faq.question: Which platforms can it document?
faq.answer: It can cover iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, watchOS, and visionOS projects.

faq.question: Can it inspect existing project files?
faq.answer: Yes. It looks for useful signals in common Apple project files and source code.

faq.question: Does it write production code?
faq.answer: No. It writes planning context and does not generate app implementation code.

faq.question: When should I use it again?
faq.answer: Use it when platforms, technologies, accessibility goals, users, or design assets change.
